description: Curated starting materials. Every entry names where its numbers came from.
disclaimer: Values marked status='indicative' are typical published figures for the grade, not design values. Grade designations cover ranges that vary with product form, temper and thickness, and a design value must come from the governing standard or the mill certificate. Check before use.

materials.name: EN AW-6082-T6
materials.notes: 0.2% proof 310 MPa and tensile 340 MPa from the supplier datasheet, which does not separate tempers; EN 1999-1-1 characteristic values for design are lower and depend on product form and thickness. Poisson ratio 0.33 is the conventional value for wrought aluminium. No hardening curve: none was available from a citable source.

materials.name: EN 1.4404 (316L)
materials.notes: Modulus 200 GPa and density 8000 kg/m3 from the supplier datasheet. 0.2% proof 220 MPa is the commonly quoted characteristic value for the grade; EN 10088-3 gives 500-700 MPa tensile, and the lower bound is used here. Austenitic stainless has markedly non-linear behaviour well below the proof stress, so a linear-elastic idealisation is conservative in stiffness terms only. No hardening curve: none was available from a citable source.
